KuroganeOS 6.0.0-dev — Core Steel / Kernel Core 2.0 candidate

This media moves the Road-to-15 development identity to Core Steel. It is a
development candidate, not a stable release and not a claim of broad physical
hardware qualification.

Implemented Core Steel scope:
- Scheduler 2.0 policy with per-CPU run queues, affinity, priorities,
  round-robin tie breaking and work stealing;
- scheduler topology expansion after SMP discovery without dropping BSP
  runnable state;
- atomic Ready -> Running dispatch reservation under the scheduler policy lock;
- CPU-owned dispatch cancellation so failed execution-layer handoff cannot
  strand a runnable thread;
- thread/process integration with scheduler policy state transitions;
- per-CPU scheduler stack / preemption return state for x86-64 SMP execution;
- dedicated Local APIC scheduling interrupt path and timer primitives;
- existing four-vCPU AP startup, cross-CPU work and TLB shootdown preserved.

Qualification boundary:
The 6.0 identity means Kernel Core 2.0 engineering is now the active system
milestone. Final qualification still requires the exact candidate Core Steel
closeout to pass host regressions, a clean release-media build and four-vCPU
QEMU runtime checks for Scheduler 2.0 topology, kernel preemption, Ring-3
preemption and the existing SMP substrate.

Oracle VirtualBox, VMware and physical Intel/AMD systems remain external
validation targets. Their absence is never converted into a fabricated PASS.
